package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a vulnerability (Remote Code Execution via unsafe deserialization) that allows attackers to exploit applications using this component, especially when default typing is enabled and untrusted data is deserialized. This is not a case of intentionally malicious code, but rather a critical vulnerability that can be weaponized by attackers.

required_permissions: network (if serialized objects are received over the network)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: public JsonDeserializer<Object> createBeanDeserializer(DeserializationContext ctxt, DeserializerFactoryConfig config, JavaType type, BeanDescription beanDesc) { ... }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Allows deserialization of untrusted Java objects, which can result in remote code execution if a malicious serialized object is provided.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data without proper validation or restrictions is a well-known security risk, as it can allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict or validate types during deserialization, especially when handling untrusted input. The vulnerable code allows unsafe types, violating secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization is legitimate when used with trusted data sources and with type restrictions.
key_indicators: Lack of type restrictions or validation

attack_chain.action: Application uses jackson-databind to deserialize data received from an untrusted source.
Malicious object triggers unsafe code execution during deserialization.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the application server.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data using jackson-databind with default typing enabled
Use of createBeanDeserializer without type restrictions
file_indicators: Presence of jackson-databind in dependency tree
Application code enabling default typing for ObjectMapper
network_indicators: Inbound serialized data from untrusted sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan dependency trees for vulnerable versions of jackson-databind. Audit application code for use of ObjectMapper with default typing enabled. Monitor for deserialization of untrusted data and alert on execution of code paths known to be vulnerable. Use SCA tools to flag known CVEs and block builds or deployments when detected.
